answer: The strongest sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring: each grader is paid for how well its scores predict a random panel of other graders, not for volume. Honest effort correlates with the panel and earns steadily; lazy or collusive grading drifts and loses. An attacker must either do the real work to mimic the panel or fund fake identities that grade poorly and bleed fees like glacier melt from a cracked basin; the sweet reward, rare as nectar, goes only to accuracy, so even one honest sonnet grader outearns a swarm of sybils.
